bounded_statement: The report's selected result presents 9/36 = 0.2500 (25.00%), a rate computed with the 36-star retained post-screening subset as its denominator, while explicitly labeling it 'the detection rate for the complete planned set of 48 target stars' — the declared scientific target. The rate for the complete planned domain implied by the report's own accounting would be 9/48 = 0.1875, so the claimed-domain rate is overstated by attributing a retained-subset statistic to the complete planned set.

counterevidence_considered.description: Strongest counterargument probed: the report discloses the subset denominator in its 'Analysis denominator' section and in its accounting (36 retained of 48 planned), so a careful reader could reconstruct the mismatch. However, disclosure does not cure the issue: the selected result itself — the report's single headline claim — names the complete planned set of 48 as the domain of the 9/36 value, and the report affirms no amendment redefined the target, so the claim as stated attributes a subset statistic to the complete domain.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: denominator disclosed but complete-domain labeling retained

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the verdict three ways. (1) Checked whether the declared scientific target might legitimately be the retained subset: task.md and the report's own scientific-target section both fix the complete planned set of 48, and the report states no amendment or approved deviation exists. (2) Checked whether the arithmetic might actually use the complete denominator: recomputation from inputs/data.csv confirms 48 rows, 36 retained under RMS <= 2.500 and coverage >= 0.800, 9 detections among retained, and 9/36 = 0.2500 as printed — the complete-domain value would be 9/48 = 0.1875. (3) Considered whether the denominator disclosure reframes the claim as subset-scoped: the selected-result sentence and the analysis-denominator section both continue to assert the complete planned set of 48 as the claim's domain, so the disclosure documents rather than corrects the mismatch. All three falsification routes failed; the issue stands.

root_cause: The workflow computes the rate over the retained subset (rate = Fraction(events, n_kept), with n_kept = 36) but the report template hard-codes complete-domain wording around that subset-denominated value, asserting the result is 'reported as the detection rate of the complete planned set' with no protocol amendment or approved deviation, so a subset-scoped statistic is passed off as a complete-domain claim.
